questions.question:
Direction: **Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.**

**A: **While the most common belief is that these traits remain fixed, research studies show otherwise.

**B:** One such research study suggests that we can change our traits provided we want to change them.

**C:** We all possess certain personality traits that set us apart from the rest.

**D:** These traits, a mix of good and bad, define how we respond to situations and people.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"CDAB**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• While arranging the parts of the sentence given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them__, so let’s find out.
 
• Part ‘A’ starts with the conjunction 'while'.
 
• Let us see some information about "While":
 __
 
• **"While"** is not used only used to introduce adverbial clauses of time. 
 
• In more formal usage, it is used to link or balance ideas that contrast each other:
 
 
 
• Part ‘B’ is providing the conclusion, and Part **'C' **is directly connected to Part **'D'**.
 
 
• Therefore the starting part is Part ‘C’.
 
 
 
• Part ‘D’ is the successor of Part **'C'** with as Part **'D'** is explaining about traits which are discussed in Part** 'C'**.
 
 
• Therefore, Part ‘D’ follows Part ‘C’.
 
 
 
• Part ‘A’ is giving further information about the subject.
 
 
• Therefore, Part ‘A’ follows Part ‘D’.
 
 
 
• Part ‘B’ is providing a conclusion to the context.
 
 
• **Therefore, Part ‘B’ follows Part 'A'.**
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct order is "CDAB__".​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Let us see the meaning of the word "Possess":**:

 
 
• ​**Possess:** have as belonging to one; own.
 
 
 
• Let us look at the sentence with the word "Possess"::
 
 
• *​I do not **possess** a television set.*

questions.question:
**Direction: Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence**

The manager said, “I want you to attend the conference.”

options.text: The manager said that she wanted me to attend the conference.
The manager said that she want me to attend the conference.
The manager told to me I am to go to attend the conference.
The manager said I am wanting you to attend the conference.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"__The manager said that she wanted me to attend the conference__"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Necessary steps to form the indirect form of the given sentence are as follows:**

 
 
• Omit all inverted commas or quotation marks.
 
• **'That'** is inserted after the helping verb of the subject.
 
• Here, the helping verb after the subject **"The manager"** is **"said"**.
 
• End the sentence with a full stop.
 
• Use pronouns appropriately.
 
• If the verb inside the inverted commas/quotation marks is in the present tense, change it into the corresponding past tense. 
 
• In this question, the given Direct Speech is in 'Present Simple' Tense, so it will be changed to 'Past Simple' Tense for Indirect Speech.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **"The manager said that she wanted me to attend the conference"***.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**​

 
• **Let us understand the meaning of "Conference":**

 
 
• **Conference: **a formal meeting of people with a shared interest, typically one that takes place over several days.
 
 
 
• **Example: **
 
 
• *An international **conference** on the environment was conducted.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank**

You've cleared the _________ examination, haven't you?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'entrance'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word of the given fill in the blank is **'entrance'. **
 
• We know that the most appropriate phrase is **'Entrance examination'. **We know that **the entrance examination is cleared. **
 
• **Entrance exams** are the ones that we take to be accepted into a school, etc. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 

**Correct Answer:__** You've cleared the **entrance **examination, haven't you?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The given sentence is an example of **a question tag. **Some rules of the question tag as follows: 
 
• If the verb is in the past simple we use did. 
 
 
• *Example: They went to the cinema, didn't they?*
 
 
 
• When the statement contains a word with a negative meaning, the question tag needs to be positive. 
 
 
• *Example: They rarely eat in restaurants, do they?*
 
• In the above example 'rarely' is a negative word. Therefore, a positive question tag will be used.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of work I __would be doing__ before.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'had been doing'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is **grammatically incorrect. **
 
• The correct answer is **Option 4 **because the doctor is assuring that the person would recover and would be able to do the work that he had been doing before/for a long time.
 
• **The past perfect continuous tense **(also known as the past perfect progressive tense) shows that **an action that started in the past continued up until another time in the past.** The past perfect continuous tense is constructed using **had been + the verb’s present participle (root + -ing). **
 
• And we also know that **'before'** used to connect earlier events to the moment of speaking or** to a point of time in the past. **
 
 
• *Example: I introduced Tom to Olivia last night. They hadn’t met before. (up to that point in the past)*
 
 
 
• Here, in the given question** 'before'** is used **'to a point of time in the past.' **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** My doctor knew that I would eventually recover and do the kind of word I **had been doing** before. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The structure of Present Perfect Continuous:

 
 
• Subject+has/have+been+v1+ing+object+since/for+time. 

 
 
• ​Example: *Monika has been waiting here for two hours.*

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Out of the given options, pick the one that gives their correct order.**

A. Vijay, the bus conductor, was always there in one of these trucks.

B. He had now quit his old job and joined politics.

C. In the week before the elections, trucks bumped up and down the dirty streets of Laxmangarh, full of young men holding microphones and shouting: "Stand up to the rich!"

D. That was the thing about Vijay; each time you saw him, he had done better to himself.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'CABD.' **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of Sentence Jumble. 
 
• We know that the first statement of a sentence jumbled question is usually an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, starting of an incident, or it starts with 'most' or 'once'. 
 
• Here, in the given question **Part C** will be the first sentence because **it is the starting of an incident.*** 'In the week before the elections, trucks bumped up...' *the given sentence is clearly talking about **an election rally.** Therefore, it will be **the first sentence. **
 
• **Part C i**s talking about the* 'trucks bumped up and down...'.* It is talking about *'Vijay who was a bus conductor, and he was always there'. *
 
• **Part C** will be the next sentence because **Part A** tells us about the old job of** 'VIjay'** and he joined **politics**. Therefore, it will be the next sentence. 
 
• **Part D** will come last because it concludes who **'Vijay'** is. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *In the week before the elections, trucks bumped up and down the dirty streets of Laxmangarh, full of young men holding microphones and shouting: "Stand up to the rich!". Vijay, the bus conductor, was always there in one of these trucks. He had now quit his old job and joined politics. That was the thing about Vijay; each time you saw him, he had done better to himself.*

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive form of the given sentence**

My friend narrated a very interesting story at the International Storytelling Festival.

options.text: A very interesting story has been narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story is being narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story was narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.
A very interesting story was being narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'A very interesting story was narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.' **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Active Voice.** As per the given question we have to change it into **Passive Voice. **
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• **'My friend' **is** the subject** of the given sentence. 
 
• **The object **of the given sentence is **'A very interesting story'. **
 
• The subject will be put in place of the object and the object will be put in place of the subject. 
 
• **'Narrated'** will be changed into **'was narrated'.** We know that in **Active to Passive transformation** **second form of verb** is changed into **'Was+V₃'. **
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__ ***A very interesting story was narrated by my friend at the International Storytelling Festival.​ *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Transformation of Infinitives: 

 
 
• Subject+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+V1+Object. (Active Voice)
 
• Subject (objective case)+is/am/are/was/were/has/have/had+to+be+V3+by+object (Subjective case). (Passive Voice)
 
 
• *Example:*
 
 
• *The teacher is to solve the doubt of every student. *
 
• *The doubt of every student is to be solved by the teacher. *

The student has made lodged a __________ with the police about a false video of her that is being circulated by some miscreants.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'complaint'. **

***__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate word to the given fill in the blank is **'complaint'. **
 
• We know that** Complaint **is **the noun.** Usually referred to in official terms. Basically means a grievance or issue against a person.
 
 
• *Example: He filed a formal **complaint **about his rude behaviour in class.*
 
 
 
• Whereas,** ''complain'**' is** a verb **and denotes an action done by the complaint. It means to express grievance against an issue or happening.
 
• And we know that after the **article 'a' **we should use a **noun. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3.** 

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** complaint. *

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

DEROGATORY
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Disparaging'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate synonym of the given word is** 'Disparaging'.** 
 
• Let's look at the meaning and examples of the given options: 

 

 
 

 **Derogatory**
 showing strong disapproval and not showing respect
 *He made some **derogatory **comment about her appearance.*
 
 

 **Lethargic**
 having little energy; feeling unwilling and unable to do anything
 *I was feeling tired and **lethargic**.*
 
 

 **Disparaging**
 to criticize someone or something in a way that shows you do not respect or value him, her, or it
 *The actor's work for charity has recently been **disparaged **in the press as an attempt to get publicity.*
 
 

 **Appreciative**
 showing that you understand how good something is, or are grateful for something
 *I'm very **appreciative **of all the support you've given me.*
 
 

 **Favourable**
 showing that you like or approve of someone or something
 *We have had a **favourable **response to the plan so far.*
 
 

 

 
• Therefore, by reading the above explanation we find that the correct answer is **Option 2. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *Disparaging. *

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error**

A Delhi bound aircraft has to make an emergency landing at Mumbai airport as a woman passenger suddenly developed a serious breathing problem.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'has to make'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous Part **'has to make'** should be **'had to make'. **
 
• We know that the given sentence is in **the past tense. **
 
• And **'Had to'** is used to talk about necessity and obligation that existed in** the past.** **'Had to'** is the past tense form of **'have to'. **
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1. **

 ​

**Correct Answer:__** *A Delhi-bound aircraft **had to make **an emergency landing at Mumbai airport as a woman passenger suddenly developed a serious breathing problem.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The following phrases are followed by past indefinite/simple tense:

 
 
• It's high time, It's Time, It's about time, etc.

 
 
• Example: *It's high time I started preparing for the exam in Hindi Literature.*
